name: GET /api/analytics/overview - lead response-time and conversion analytics
description: Returns the analytics rollup the Analytics Dashboard renders: the capture-to-response funnel, the conversion rates between its stages, the response-time distribution, and a per-source-channel breakdown plus a per-day series. A read, so it answers 200. THIS IS NOT GET /api/sla/status. That endpoint is OPERATIONAL - a live triage view answering 'which clocks need somebody right now', with an attention list of open at-risk and breached leads. This one is ANALYTICAL - it answers 'how are we performing and where', aggregated over a closed historical window, with no per-lead rows at all. The two deliberately compute different things and neither is derivable from the other. FUNNEL: captured counts every lead that arrived in the window; routed counts those that reached an owner (leads.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL); responded counts those a human answered (leads.first_response_at IS NOT NULL); breached counts leads.sla_breached. CONVERSION RATES are stage-to-stage, each expressed 0..1 rounded to four decimals: routed_rate is routed/captured, response_rate is responded/routed, and breach_rate is breached over leads whose clock has CLOSED. Every rate is NULL rather than 0 when its denominator is empty - reporting a rate of zero for a window with nothing in it is a number a manager would act on, and the dashboard renders null as an em dash instead. RESPONSE TIMES are seconds from lead ARRIVAL (leads.created_at), not from assignment, matching POST /api/leads/:id/first-response: the prospect has been waiting since they submitted, and measuring from assignment would let a lead sit unrouted for an hour and still report a fast response. average, median and p90 are reported together because an average alone hides the tail that actually loses deals; all three are null when nothing in the window has been responded to. FILTERS: from and to bound the window by lead arrival (ISO 8601; to must be after from; the range is capped at 366 days); source narrows to one capture channel; owner_user_id narrows to one representative's queue. All four are optional and combine; omitting from and to reports the last 30 days. Protected by the authenticate guard - the Authorization header is required on this GET. QA: depends on register (which creates the user passed as owner_user_id), login, and a captured lead so the window is non-empty. The malformed-owner_user_id branch is documented in errorCases but has no automated case: owner_user_id is a foreign key, and MUST-36 requires every FK value to come from a captured producer value rather than a literal, so a deliberately malformed id cannot be expressed here. The 400 path is exercised by the inverted-window and unknown-source cases instead, and validateUuidParam itself is covered where it is used on a path param.

testCases.name: Read the analytics overview for a bounded window
Reject a window whose end is before its start
Reject a source outside the capture-channel vocabulary

errorCases.when: from or to is present but not a parseable ISO 8601 date, to is not after from, the range exceeds 366 days, source is present but not one of the fourteen capture channels, or owner_user_id is present but not a well-formed UUID
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
